This structural similarity may explain the observed binding affinity and functional interaction between Dexfenfluramine and Cyp2a6. The shared pharmacological profile of these compounds, combined with their binding to Cyp2a6, implies that Dexfenfluramine could act as a modulator of Cyp2a6 activity, potentially influencing the metabolism of arachidonic acid and other substrates.

The integration of these pathways highlights a possible mechanism by which Dexfenfluramine interacts with Cyp2a6, involving both direct binding and indirect effects through shared metabolic pathways. The evidence supports a role for Dexfenfluramine in modulating Cyp2a6 activity, likely through its structural similarity to other compounds that bind to this enzyme.
